captions.linkedin:
Every CTA worth its fee runs commodity momentum. Here's the published version they're not advertising.

Miffre & Rallis, Journal of Banking & Finance (2007). They tested 31 US commodity futures across 1979-2004 and ran 56 long-short momentum specifications.

13 of those specs were profitable. The average: +9.38% annualized.

The mechanic (the boring, durable one):

🔹 RANK ~20-35 LIQUID COMMODITY FUTURES by trailing 12-month return
🔹 LONG the top quintile (winners)
🔹 SHORT the bottom quintile (losers)
🔹 DOLLAR-NEUTRAL, equal-weight within quintiles
🔹 MONTHLY REBALANCE
🔹 SECTORS: energy, metals, grains, softs, livestock

The term-structure link: winners tend to be in backwardation (front-month richer than deferred), losers tend to be in contango. The momentum signal is partly proxying for the carry already embedded in the futures curve.

Why this matters to a stock-and-bond portfolio: documented low correlation to equities AND bonds. It's the diversifying sleeve that actually diversifies.

Why retail misses it: most retail platforms don't make rolling 20+ commodity futures easy. The funds have the back-office to do it. You can too, with the right system.

Strategy shared free. Performance depends on execution, sizing, and risk gates, that's the part we engineer.
